Based on the retrieved healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that the distance to a high-volume center may be worth it for patients who travel long distances. Specifically, our results indicate that:

* Patients who traveled a long distance to a high-volume center had improved lymph node yield, neoadjuvant chemoradiation receipt, and 30- and 90-day mortality compared with those who traveled a short distance.
* They also had improved 5-year survival.
* This suggests that the increased distance may be worth it for patients who are willing to travel further to receive specialized care.

It's essential to note that this does not mean that all patients traveling long distances will benefit, and more intensive efforts at early detection of cancer in remote areas may be needed. Additionally, other factors such as timely diagnosis and treatment, rather than just distance, play a crucial role in determining the effectiveness of medical interventions.
